h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ד׳ Pesach — Maamar Daled
Pesach of Egypt and Pesach of Generations: Passing Over and Eliminating Chametz

p: אִיתָא בַּמִּשְׁנָה
It is stated in the Mishnah
(פְּסָחִים צ"ו.):
(Pesachim 96a):
מַה בֵּין פֶּסַח מִצְרַיִם לְפֶסַח דּוֹרוֹת וְכוּלֵּי?
"What is the difference between the Pesach of Egypt and the Pesach of future generations, etc.?
פֶּסַח מִצְרַיִם נֶאֱכָל בְּלַיְלָה אַחַת, וּפֶסַח דּוֹרוֹת כָּל שִׁבְעָה.
The Pesach of Egypt is eaten on one night, whereas the Pesach of future generations is all seven."
וְהִנֵּה גַּם פֶּסַח דּוֹרוֹת נֶאֱכָל רַק לַיְלָה אַחַת!
Now, the Pesach offering of future generations is also eaten only on one night!
וּבַגְּמָרָא שָׁם מְתָרֵץ דְּקָאֵי עַל אִיסּוּר חָמֵץ,
And in the Gemara there it answers that it refers to the prohibition of chametz:
דְּפֶסַח מִצְרַיִם חִימּוּצוֹ נוֹהֵג רַק יוֹם אֶחָד, וּפֶסַח דּוֹרוֹת חִימּוּצוֹ נוֹהֵג כָּל שִׁבְעָה.
that at the Pesach of Egypt its chametz prohibition applied only for one day, whereas at the Pesach of future generations its chametz prohibition applies all seven days.
אֲבָל שִׁטְחִיּוּת לְשׁוֹן הַמִּשְׁנָה נִרְאֶה דְּקָאֵי עַל קָרְבַּן פֶּסַח!
Yet on the surface, the wording of the Mishnah appears to refer to the Pesach sacrifice itself!
וְהִנֵּה בְּפָרָשַׁת רְאֵה נֶאֱמַר
Now in Parshas Re'eh it is said
(דְּבָרִים ט"ז, ג'):
(Devarim 16:3):
לֹא תֹאכַל עָלָיו חָמֵץ, שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת.
"You shall not eat chametz with it (alav); seven days you shall eat matzos with it (alav)."
וְ"עָלָיו" הַיְינוּ עַל הַקָּרְבַּן פֶּסַח
And "with it (alav)" refers to the Pesach offering
וּמַה עִנְיַן שִׁבְעָה יָמִים שֶׁל אֲכִילַת מַצָּה עַל הַקָּרְבַּן פֶּסַח,
yet what is the connection of seven days of eating matzah to the Pesach offering,
וַהֲלוֹא גַּם בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה אֲכִילַת מַצָּה שִׁבְעָה יָמִים?!
when even nowadays eating matzah applies for seven days?!
וְגַם מַה זֶּה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר זֹאת לְהַקְדָּמָה לְמִצְוַת קִידּוּשׁ בְּכוֹרִים,
And also, why was this stated as an introduction to the mitzvah of sanctifying the firstborn,
שֶׁאַחַר מַאֲמַר ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ: קַדֶּשׁ לִי כָל בְּכוֹר, אָמַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִקּוֹדֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
that after the utterance of Hashem, may He be blessed, "Sanctify to Me every firstborn," Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, first said to Israel:
לֹא יֵאָכֵל חָמֵץ, הַיּוֹם אַתֶּם יוֹצְאִים וְגוֹמֵר
"No chametz shall be eaten; today you are going out, etc."
שֶׁבְּמִצְרַיִם נוֹהֵג רַק יוֹם אֶחָד, וּלְדוֹרוֹת נוֹהֵג כָּל שִׁבְעָה?
that in Egypt it applied only one day, whereas for generations it applies all seven?
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר בָּזֶה:
And one may explain this as follows:
דְּהִנֵּה עִיקַּר עִנְיַן קָרְבַּן פֶּסַח הוּא שֶׁפָּסַח הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל בָּתֵּי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
behold, the core essence of the Pesach offering is that the Holy One, blessed is He, passed over the houses of the Children of Israel
וְלֹא יִתֵּן הַמַּשְׁחִית לָבֹא אֶל בָּתֵּיכֶם.
"and did not allow the Destroyer to enter your houses."
וְהַמַּשְׁחִית יָדוּעַ שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂטָן, הוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת, וְהוּא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁבַּנֶּפֶשׁ הַמַּסִּית וּמַדִּיחַ וְעוֹלֶה וּמְקַטְרֵג וְכוּלֵּי,
And the Destroyer, as is known, is Satan, is the Angel of Death, and is the evil inclination within the soul that entices, misleads, ascends, and prosecutes, etc.,
וְהוּא הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה.
and it is the leaven in the dough.
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּקְּעוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם בְּסִיבָּתוֹ בְּאַרְבָּעִים וְתֵשַׁע שַׁעֲרֵי טוּמְאָה,
And because our ancestors sank in Egypt on its account into the forty-nine gates of impurity,
מִזֶּה עַצְמוֹ הָיָה הַקִּטְרוּג גָּדוֹל מְאֹד: מַה נִּשְׁתַּנּוּ אֵלּוּ מֵאֵלּוּ?
from that very fact there was a massive prosecution: "How are these different from those?"
עַד שֶׁכִּבְיָכוֹל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בִּכְבוֹדוֹ וּבְעַצְמוֹ הוּצְרַךְ לַעֲמוֹד עַל הַפֶּתַח לְהוֹשִׁיעָם מִכַּף מְעַוֵּל וְחוֹמֵץ.
So much so that, as it were, the Holy One, blessed is He, in His glory and essence had to stand at the doorway to save them from the grasp of the wrongdoer and oppressor.
וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן נוֹהֵג גַּם לְדוֹרוֹת כַּאֲשֶׁר מַקְרִיבִין הַפֶּסַח,
And this very dynamic applies for all generations as well whenever they offer the Pesach sacrifice,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(שְׁמוֹת י"ב, כ"ז):
(Shemos 12:27):
וַאֲמַרְתֶּם זֶבַח פֶּסַח הוּא לַה' אֲשֶׁר פָּסַח עַל בָּתֵּי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹמֵר
"And you shall say, 'It is a Pesach offering to Hashem, Who passed over the houses of the Children of Israel, etc.'"
שֶׁכִּבְיָכוֹל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מְרַחֵם עַל כָּל פְּרָטֵי נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁתַּקְּעוּ בְּעוֹמֶק הַשִּׁפְלוּת מִצַּד הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה,
for, as it were, Hashem, may He be blessed, has mercy on every individual soul of Israel that has sunk into the depths of lowliness due to the leaven in the dough,
לַעֲמוֹד לִימִין אֶבְיוֹן לְהוֹשִׁיעַ מִשֹּׁפְטֵי נַפְשׁוֹ.
"standing at the right hand of the needy, to save him from those who judge his soul."
וְעַל זֶה נִיתַּן גַּם כֵּן הַמִּצְוָה לְהַשְׁבִּית הַשְּׂאוֹר וְהֶחָמֵץ מִצַּד הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
And alongside this was also given the mitzvah to eliminate leaven and chametz from the soul's side,
שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁל פְּגַם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל תַּאֲוַת אֲכִילָה
which is the primary evil inclination of the original blemish of the lust for eating,
וְגַם כָּל מִינֵי תַּאֲווֹת הַגּוּף שֶׁהוּא הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה.
as well as all forms of bodily desires, which constitute the leaven in the dough.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ
And concerning this they said
(בְּרָכוֹת ל"ד.)
(Berachos 34a)
שֶׁהַשְּׂאוֹר מִיעוּטוֹ יָפֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
that a small amount of leaven is beneficial, as brought in the holy Zohar
(מִדְרָשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם חֵלֶק א' קל"ח.),
(Midrash HaNe'elam, Vol. 1, 138a),
שֶׁיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה נִקְרָא לָבָן שֶׁיִּתְלַבֵּן לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא,
that the evil inclination of desire is called "Lavan" (white) because it will be whitened in the future to come,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבְּעֶצֶם הַיֵּצֶר נִבְרָא לַחֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
since in its essence the inclination was created for yearning after Torah, as it is said
(דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א' כ"ט, י"ח):
(I Divrei HaYamim 29:18):
שָׁמְרָה זֹּאת לְעוֹלָם לְיֵצֶר מַחְשְׁבוֹת לְבַב וְגוֹמֵר,
"Keep this forever as the inclination of the thoughts of the heart, etc."
רַק מַה שֶּׁהָאָדָם עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ רַע לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בּוֹ לְחֶמְדַּת הַבְלֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
only man makes it evil by using it to covet the vanities of this world.
וְלָכֵן בְּעַצֶּרֶת מַקְרִיבִין שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם שֶׁל חָמֵץ,
And therefore on Shavuos we offer the Two Loaves of chametz,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבִּזְמַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה נִכְנְסוּ חֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא בְּנֶפֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
because at the time of the Giving of the Torah, yearning for Torah entered the soul of Israel,
וְאָז הַשְּׂאוֹר יָפֶה לַנֶּפֶשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
and then leaven is beneficial for the soul, as they said
(סוּכָּה נ"ב:):
(Sukkah 52b):
אִם פָּגַע בְּךָ מְנוּוָּל זֶה
"If this repulsive one encounters you"
כִּינּוּי לְיֵצֶר הָרָע שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה
a reference to the evil inclination of desire
מָשְׁכֵהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
"drag him to the study hall,"
יַכְנִיס אֶת הַחֶמְדָּה זוֹ בְּעֶצֶם לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
where he will channel this very desire into words of Torah.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּחַג הַמַּצּוֹת, שֶׁאָז הַמִּצְוָה בְּלֶחֶם עֹנִי
Not so on Chag HaMatzos, when the mitzvah is with "bread of poverty (oni)"
וְאֵין עָנִי אֶלָּא בְּדַעַת וְכוּלֵּי
and "there is no poverty except in knowledge, etc."
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנַס הַדַּעַת בַּנֶּפֶשׁ לְבָרֵר הַטּוֹב, הוּצְרַךְ לְבַעֵר הַשְּׂאוֹר וְהֶחָמֵץ מִנַּפְשׁוֹ מִכֹּל וָכֹל,
and as long as knowledge has not yet entered the soul to sift out the good, one must completely eliminate leaven and chametz from his soul;
וְזֶהוּ מִצְוַת אֲכִילַת מַצָּה בְּלֵיל רִאשׁוֹן מִצַּד הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הָאָדָם בְּנַפְשׁוֹ.
and this is the mitzvah of eating matzah on the first night from the side of man's awakening within his soul.
וְעִם כָּל זֶה, אִם אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזֵר לוֹ אֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ,
And with all this, if the Holy One, blessed is He, does not help him, he cannot overcome it,
שֶׁעֶצֶם הַכֹּחַ הַזֶּה נִשְׁפַּע עָלָיו מִלְּמַעְלָה מִצַּד הַפֶּסַח כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
for this very strength flows upon him from above by virtue of the Pesach offering, as mentioned above.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר בְּפָרָשַׁת רְאֵה: תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת
And regarding this it is said in Parshas Re'eh: "You shall eat matzos upon/with it (alav)"
"עָלָיו" דַּיְיקָא, שֶׁמִּכֹּחַ הַפֶּסַח נִשְׁפַּע עַל הַנֶּפֶשׁ כֹּחַ לְהַשְׁבִּית הַשְּׂאוֹר מִנַּפְשׁוֹ בִּקְדוּשַּׁת אֲכִילַת הַמַּצָּה.
specifically "upon it," meaning that from the power of the Pesach offering, strength flows into the soul to eliminate the leaven from oneself through the holiness of eating matzah.
וְגַם בְּדוֹרוֹתֵינוּ אֵלֶּה שֶׁאֵין לָנוּ מִקְדָּשׁ לְהַקְרִיב הַפֶּסַח,
And even in these generations of ours when we have no Temple in which to offer the Pesach sacrifice,
הַקִּיוּוּי שֶׁל כָּל נֶפֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר מְצַפָּה לָזֶה, שֶׁאִם הָיָה בִּיכוֹלֶת בְּכָל לִבּוֹ וְנַפְשׁוֹ הָיָה מוּכָן לְהַקְרִיב הַפֶּסַח,
the yearning of every Jewish soul that longs for this—such that if it were possible, with all his heart and soul he would be ready to offer the Pesach sacrifice
הֲרֵי זֶה חָשׁוּב לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרַבְנוּ הַפֶּסַח לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁפַּע קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ זֹאת עָלֵינוּ כְּמֵאָז,
this is reckoned before Hashem, may He be blessed, as though we actually offered the Pesach sacrifice, so that its holiness flows upon us just as in days of old,
וְרַחֲמָנָא לִיבָּא בָּעֵי.
for "the Merciful One desires the heart."
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן הַמִּשְׁנָה בֵּין פֶּסַח מִצְרַיִם לְפֶסַח דּוֹרוֹת:
And concerning this it is stated in the wording of the Mishnah comparing the Pesach of Egypt and the Pesach of future generations:
שֶׁחִימּוּצוֹ יוֹם אֶחָד, וּפֶסַח דּוֹרוֹת כָּל שִׁבְעָה
that its chametz prohibition was one day, whereas the Pesach of future generations is all seven
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָנוּ יוֹדְעִים בְּנַפְשֵׁינוּ שֶׁכָּל הַכֹּחַ שֶׁלָּנוּ שֶׁל אֲכִילַת מַצָּה וְהַשְׁבָּתַת שְׂאוֹר מִנַּפְשֵׁינוּ
because we know within our souls that our entire strength for eating matzah and eliminating leaven from our souls
הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁנִּשְׁפַּע מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כֹּחַ הַפְּסִיחָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
comes solely from the power of "passing over" bestowed by Hashem, may He be blessed, as mentioned above.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן בִּלְשׁוֹן חֲזַ"ל נִקְרָא "חַג הַפֶּסַח" עַל רֶמֶז זֶה,
And likewise, in the terminology of our Sages, of blessed memory, it is called "Chag HaPesach" based on this allusion:
וְאָנוּ קוֹרִין הֶחָג עַל שֵׁם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁהַכֹּל מִצִּדּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ;
we name the festival after the Holy One, blessed is He, acknowledging that everything comes from His side, may He be blessed;
וּבִלְשׁוֹן הַתּוֹרָה נִקְרָא בְּשֵׁם "חַג הַמַּצּוֹת",
whereas in the terminology of the Torah it is called "Chag HaMatzos,"
כִּי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ קוֹרְאוֹ עַל שֵׁם מַעֲשֵׂינוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה הַכֹּל מִצִּדֵּנוּ.
because Hashem, may He be blessed, names it after our deeds, as though everything were accomplished from our side.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 3 — “Pesach is called in the Torah ‘Chag HaMatzos’ and in the language of the Sages ‘Chag HaPesach’: the Sages named it for the praise of Hashem, Who passed over Israel's houses, and Hashem in the Written Torah named it for the praise of Israel, Chag HaMatzos, the nullifying of the leaven in the dough from Israel's side. So here, in the language of the Sages in the Oral Torah, Shavuos is called Atzeres, after the absorbing of the holiness of Pesach at the Giving of the Torah; and Hashem in the Written Torah calls it Shavuos, after the seven weeks, which is Israel's praise.” Connection: The same reading of the two names of Pesach, Hashem's praise in the Sages' name and Israel's in the Torah's; Shavuos 3 carries the pattern over to Atzeres and Shavuos.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushas Levi, Bo — “One must understand why we call the festival that the Torah names Chag HaMatzos by the name Pesach. It is written, ‘I am my Beloved's and my Beloved is mine’: we tell the praise of the Holy One, blessed is He, and the Holy One, blessed is He, tells the praise of Israel; so too with the tefillin we wear and the tefillin He wears. Chag HaMatzos is named for the praise of Israel, who baked the dough as cakes of matzah, as Rashi explains that the verse tells the praise of Israel; therefore in the Torah the festival is called Chag HaMatzos, as though the Blessed One tells the praise of Israel. And we call it Pesach, for the praise of the Blessed One, ‘who passed over the houses of the Children of Israel.’” Connection: The Kedushas Levi gives the same reading of the festival's two names; he sets it within the mutual praise of Israel and Hashem, as in their exchange of tefillin.

p: וְהִנֵּה בְּפֶסַח מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהָיָה הַיְּצִיאָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מִתַּכְלִית עוֹמֶק הַשִּׁפְלוּת,
Now at the Pesach of Egypt, which was the initial emergence from the utmost depth of lowliness,
וְהָיוּ עוֹד בְּלִי תוֹרָה וּבְלִי מִצְווֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
when they were still without Torah and without mitzvos, as it is said
(יְחֶזְקֵאל ט"ז, ז'):
(Yechezkel 16:7):
וְאַתְּ עֵרֹם וְעֶרְיָה,
"Yet you were naked and bare,"
הָיָה הוֹפָעַת הֶאָרַת הַפֶּסַח מַסְפִּיק רַק עַל יוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
the shining forth of the illumination of Pesach sufficed only for the first day;
וְלָכֵן אֵין חִימּוּצוֹ נוֹהֵג רַק יוֹם אֶחָד, שֶׁזֶּה תָּלוּי בָּזֶה,
and therefore its chametz prohibition applied only for one day, as one depends on the other,
וְהַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת מִדַּת אַהֲבָה, חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם.
which is the aspect of the attribute of love, "Kindness to Avraham."
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר
And concerning this it is said
(יִרְמְיָה ב', ב'):
(Yirmiyahu 2:2):
זָכַרְתִּי לָךְ חֶסֶד נְעוּרַיִךְ וְגוֹמֵר
"I remember for you the kindness of your youth, etc."
עַל הַזְּמַן הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם.
referring to the initial moment of the Exodus from Egypt.
וְעַל זֶה רוֹמֵז בְּפָרָשַׁת קַדֶּשׁ לִי וְגוֹמֵר:
And to this it alludes in Parshas Kadesh Li, etc.:
זָכוֹר אֶת הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה וְגוֹמֵר וְלֹא יֵאָכֵל חָמֵץ הַיּוֹם וְגוֹמֵר.
"Remember this day, etc., and no chametz shall be eaten; today, etc."
דְּעִנְיַן אֲכִילַת מַצָּה נִקְרָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
For the matter of eating matzah is called in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' קפ"ג:)
מֵיכְלָא דְּאַסְוָותָא,
"food of healing,"
דַּאֲכִילָה זוֹ פּוֹעֵל רְפוּאָה לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ מַכָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
for this eating effects healing for the root of the world's wound, as it is said
(יְשַׁעְיָה ל', כ"ו):
(Yeshayahu 30:26):
וּמַחַץ מַכָּתוֹ יִרְפָּא,
"And He heals the bruise of its wound,"
וְדָרְשׁוּ
which they expounded
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה י', ד'):
(Bereishis Rabbah 10:4):
מַחַץ מַכָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם.
"the bruise of the wound of the world."
וְנֶאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ:
And afterward it is said:
וְהָיָה כִי יְבִיאֲךָ וְגוֹמֵר שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצֹּת
"And it shall be when He brings you, etc., seven days you shall eat matzos"
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי בִּיאָתָם לָאָרֶץ נִתְקַדְּשׁוּ כָּל הַמַּאֲכָלִים לִהְיוֹת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
for through their entry into the Land, all foods became sanctified to exist in holiness
עַל יְדֵי הַמִּצְווֹת הַנּוֹהֲגוֹת בָּאָרֶץ, כְּמוֹ הַפְרָשַׁת תְּרוּמוֹת וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת וּשְׁאָר מִצְווֹת שֶׁל חוֹבַת הַקַּרְקַע שֶׁהֵמָּה לְתִיקּוּן הַמַּאֲכָלִים שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
through the commandments dependent on the Land, such as separating terumos and ma'asros and other agricultural mitzvos that serve to rectify foods so that they exist in holiness,
דְּזֶה תַּכְלִית הָרְפוּאָה בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ לְמַכָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם שֶׁבָּא מִתַּאֲוַת הַמַּאֲכָל.
for this is the ultimate healing at the root for the wound of the world, which stemmed from the lust for food.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצֹּת
And through this, "seven days you shall eat matzos"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּכֹחַ הוֹפָעַת קְדוּשַּׁת הַפֶּסַח עַל כָּל שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הֶחָג,
meaning that the power of the shining forth of the holiness of Pesach will extend across all seven days of the festival
עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ לְהִתְקַדֵּשׁ בַּאֲכִילַת הַמַּצָּה כָּל שִׁבְעָה יָמִים.
through the soul's awakening to sanctify itself by eating matzah all seven days.
וְנֶאֱמַר כָּאן "מַצֹּת" חָסֵר ו', שֶׁהָיוּ אָז בַּעֲנִיּוּת הַדַּעַת,
And here "matzos" is written deficiently without a Vav, because they were then in poverty of knowledge,
וְכֵן בַּפָּסוּק "בָּעֶרֶב תֹּאכְלוּ מַצֹּת" כְּתִיב חָסֵר ו',
and likewise in the verse "In the evening you shall eat matzos" it is written deficiently without a Vav,
וּשְׁאָר כָּל מַצּוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּזְכַּר בְּעִנְיַן פֶּסַח כְּתִיב מָלֵא זוּלַת אֵלּוּ
whereas all other mentions of matzos in the Torah regarding Pesach are written plene (with a Vav) except these
דְּעִיקַּר מִצְוַת לֶחֶם עֹנִי מִצַּד עֲנִיּוּת הַדַּעַת שֶׁהָיָה אָז בְּמִצְרַיִם,
for the essence of the mitzvah of "bread of poverty" comes from the poverty of knowledge that existed then in Egypt,
וְעַל זֶה עִיקַּר מִצְוַת בָּעֶרֶב תֹּאכְלוּ וְגוֹמֵר רַק עַל לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן.
and therefore the primary obligation of "In the evening you shall eat, etc." applies only to the first night.
וּכְדֵי לִרְמוֹז שֶׁגַּם כָּל כֹּחַ הָאִתְעָרוּתָא שֶׁלָּנוּ לְהִתְקַדֵּשׁ הוּא רַק מִכֹּחַ הוֹפָעַת קְדוּשָּׁה מִלְּעֵילָּא מִבְּחִינַת וּפָסַח ה' וְגוֹמֵר כִּדְבָרֵינוּ,

And in order to allude that even our entire power of awakening from below to sanctify ourselves comes solely from the power of the shining forth of holiness from above, from the aspect of "And Hashem will pass over, etc.," as we have said,
עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר בַּפָּסוּק שֶׁאַחֲרֵי זֶה:
concerning this it is said in the verse immediately following:
מַצּוֹת יֵאָכֵל אֵת שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים
"Matzos shall be eaten (ye'achel) the seven days"
וְשָׁם נֶאֱמַר "מַצּוֹת" מָלֵא ו', וְגַם "יֵאָכֵל" מֵעַצְמוֹ,
and there "matzos" is written plene with a Vav, and also "shall be eaten" in the passive form (on its own),
וְ"שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים" בְּה' הַיָּדוּעַ,
and "the seven days" with the definite article Hei,
וְהַיְינוּ הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים הַיְדוּעִים שֶׁנִּקְרָאִים יָמִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
referring to the seven known holy attributes which are called "days," as it is said
(שְׁמוֹת כ', י"א):
(Shemos 20:11):
כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה ה' וְגוֹמֵר,
"For in six days Hashem made, etc.,"
וְאוֹת ו' הַמִּילּוּי יָדוּעַ שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיּוּת הַנִּשְׁפַּע מִלְּמַעְלָה.
and the added letter Vav, as is known, is the root of vitality flowing from above.

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר לַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁגַּם כֹּחַ פְּעוּלַּת אָדָם בָּזֶה הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הוֹפָעַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִלְּעֵילָּא עַל כָּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים שֶׁהֵמָּה שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.

That is, it becomes clear to the soul that even man's power of action in this is solely through the shining forth of holiness from above across all seven days, which are the seven holy attributes, as mentioned above.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן "יֵאָכֵל", שֶׁגַּם פְּעוּלַּת הָאֲכִילָה אֵינָהּ מִצִּידֵּנוּ רַק מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And regarding this it is stated in the passive form "ye'achel" (shall be eaten), for even the act of eating is not from our own side but from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(מְלָכִים א' ו', ז'):
(I Melachim 6:7):
וְהַבַּיִת בְּהִבָּנֹתוֹ,
"And the House, when it was being built [of itself],"
וְכִדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and as stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' רכ"ב:)
עַל פָּסוּק
on the verse
(שְׁמוֹת ל"ט, ל"ב):
(Shemos 39:32):
וַתֵּכֶל עֲבוֹדַת הַמִּשְׁכָּן
"And the work of the Tabernacle was completed"
מֵאֵלָיו.
of its own accord.
וְזֶה מְרַמֵּז עַל מַעֲשֵׂי הַמִּצְווֹת הַנַּעֲשִׂים בְּכַוָּונָה רְצוּיָה:
And this alludes to mitzvah deeds performed with desirable intent:
נִתְבָּרֵר לְהַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ גָּמַר בַּעֲדֵנוּ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה לְטוֹב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
it becomes clear to the soul that Hashem, may He be blessed, completes the deed for us for good, as it is said
(תְּהִלִּים קל"ח, ח'):
(Tehillim 138:8):
ה' יִגְמֹר בַּעֲדִי וְגוֹמֵר מַעֲשֵׂי יָדֶיךָ אַל תֶּרֶף.
"Hashem will complete it for me, etc.; do not forsake the work of Your hands."
וְהִנֵּה כָּל זֶה הוּא הַקְדָּמַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַל מִצְוַת קְדוּשַּׁת בְּכוֹר,
Now all of this is the introduction of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, to Israel regarding the mitzvah of the sanctification of the firstborn;
כִּי עִיקַּר מִצְוַת קְדוּשַּׁת בְּכוֹר לְבָרֵר אֲשֶׁר קְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בְּתוֹלָדָה מְנוּקִּים מִבְּחִינַת תַּאֲוָה זוֹ,
for the essence of the mitzvah of sanctifying the firstborn is to clarify that Israel's holiness is rooted in their very birth, cleansed from this aspect of lust,
כִּי גַּם כָּל הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף שֶׁלָּהֶם הֵמָּה מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה;
for even all their physical pleasures stem from the root of holiness;
וְזֶה הָיָה תַּכְלִית הַבֵּירוּר הַנִּגְמָר לְאַחַר בִּיאַת הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּתְקַדְּשׁוּ בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַמַּאֲכָל כִּדְבָרֵינוּ.
and this was the culmination of the refinement completed after entering the Land, when they became sanctified in the holiness of food, as we have said.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר:
And regarding this it is said:
וְהָיָה כִי יְבִיאֲךָ ה' וְגוֹמֵר וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ כָל פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם,
"And it shall be when Hashem brings you, etc., you shall set apart every first issue of the womb,"
וְיֵשׁ מַאן דְּאָמַר
and there is an opinion
(בְּכוֹרוֹת ד':)
(Bechoros 4b)
שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַדְּשׁוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת בַּמִּדְבָּר עַד בּוֹאָם לָאָרֶץ, אַף שֶׁהִיא חוֹבַת הַגּוּף,
that firstborns were not sanctified in the wilderness until they entered the Land, even though it is a personal obligation,
וְהַכֹּל כִּדְבָרֵינוּ.
and all of this aligns with our words.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tzidkas HaTzaddik 1 — “The beginning of a person's entry into the service of Hashem must be in haste, as we find with the Pesach of Egypt, which was eaten in haste, and not the Pesach of later generations. For at the start, to tear oneself away from all the desires of this world to which he is bound, he must guard the moment when the will for Hashem awakens in him and hasten upon that moment to rush out of them, perhaps he will be able. Afterward he may again go calmly and slowly, as the law of the Pesach of later generations.” Connection: The same contrast of the Pesach of Egypt as the first emergence from the depth, limited to its first moment, against the Pesach of the generations; Tzidkas HaTzaddik turns it into the rule for anyone first breaking free of his desires.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 183b (Tetzaveh) — "When Israel left Egypt they did not know the root and secret of faith. The Holy One said: let Israel taste a remedy, and until they eat this remedy no other food will be seen by them. Once they ate matzah, which is the remedy [for] entering and knowing the secret of faith, He said: from now on chametz is fit for them." The matzah is called mich'la d'asvasa, food of healing.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 222b (Pekudei) — "When all the craftsmen began to do the work, that very work they began was completed by itself: they begin, and it [the Shechinah] completes the work. From where do we know? For it is written, 'And all the work of the Mishkan of the Tent of Meeting was completed.'"
